literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的明显“内陆高死亡率 发病率 与沿海高死亡率”模式。发热伴血小板减少综合征的发病率对气象因素表现出不同的敏感性,内陆传播对热波动和受日照阈值(> 200小时/月)限制的沿海动态敏感。临床严重程度的空间差异与区域病毒遗传结构的分布相关,内陆地区以A、C、D基因型共循环为主,沿海地区以B基因型为主。浙江省被确定为遗传中心,其重组频率明显高于内陆地区。 [10.1186/s40249-026-01500-2]
NP 诱导的回忆显示出混合的 Th1 相关、Th2 相关和促炎相关特征,这些特征在 疫苗 制剂中各不相同,而 Gn 糖蛋白的头域引起有限的体液和细胞反应。 [10.64898/2026.09.11.750931]
筛查揭示了多样化的病原体景观,在 16.9% 的蜱虫中总共鉴定出 14 种病原体 (395/2,333),揭示了多样化的地理分布。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2731498]
病毒感染触发 STAT1 依赖性 IRF1 上调,IRF1 与 BAK 启动子中已识别的 ISRE 位点结合,诱导 BAK 上调。 [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117968]
SFTSV 于 2010 年首次从中国严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 患者的血清中分离和鉴定,此后在中国多个省份以及韩国、日本、越南、阿拉伯联合酋长国(包括迪拜)和巴基斯坦均有报道。 [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1827915]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.headline_en: Recent Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus literature
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: A pronounced 'inland-high-incidence vs. coastal-high-fatality' pattern of SFTS was identified. The incidence of SFTS exhibited divergent sensitivities to meteorological factors, with inland transmission being sensitive to thermal fluctuations and coastal dynamics constrained by a sunshine threshold (> 200 h/month). [10.1186/s40249-026-01500-2]

NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses. [10.64898/2026.09.11.750931]
Screening revealed a diverse pathogen landscape, identifying a total of 14 pathogens in 16.9% of the ticks (395/2,333), revealing a diverse geographical distribution. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2731498]
Viral infection triggers STAT1-dependent up-regulation of IRF1, which binds to an identified ISRE site in the BAK-promoter, inducing BAK up-regulation. [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117968]

First isolated and identified in 2010 from the serum of patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in China, SFTSV has since been reported in multiple provinces across China, as well as in South Korea, Japan, Vietnam, the United Arab Emirates (including Dubai), and Pakistan. [10.3389/fcimb.2026.1827915]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的明显“内陆高死亡率 发病率 与沿海高死亡率”模式。发热伴血小板减少综合征的发病率对气象因素表现出不同的敏感性,内陆传播对热波动和受日照阈值(> 200小时/月)限制的沿海动态敏感。临床严重程度的空间差异与区域病毒遗传结构的分布相关,内陆地区以A、C、D基因型共循环为主,沿海地区以B基因型为主。浙江省被确定为遗传中心,其重组频率明显高于内陆地区。
NP 诱导的回忆显示出混合的 Th1 相关、Th2 相关和促炎相关特征,这些特征在 疫苗 制剂中各不相同,而 Gn 糖蛋白的头域引起有限的体液和细胞反应。 [10.64898/2026.09.11.750931]。
筛查揭示了多样化的病原体景观,在 16.9% 的蜱虫中总共鉴定出 14 种病原体 (395/2,333),揭示了多样化的地理分布。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2731498]。
病毒感染触发 STAT1 依赖性 IRF1 上调,IRF1 与 BAK 启动子中已识别的 ISRE 位点结合,诱导 BAK 上调。 [10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117968]。
brief_items_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
A pronounced 'inland-high-incidence vs. coastal-high-fatality' pattern of SFTS was identified.

NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses.

papers.title: Phylogeographic epidemiology of Dabie bandavirus in East Asia: divergent transmission networks and genotype‐linked clinical severity.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus (SFTSV), exhibits geographically decoupled incidence and fatality patterns across East Asia. We aimed to elucidate the distinct ecological drivers and phylogeographic dynamics underlying this inland-coastal epidemiological divergence. METHODS: Integrating 1820 high-quality global genomes of SFTSV with well-characterized clinical cohorts (936 patients) and nationwide surveillance data (27,457 cases) from China, we constructed a comprehensive analytical framework. Ecological modeling, Bayesian phylogeography, and genotype-phenotype association analyses were employed to trace the evolutionary trajectories and clinical implications of the virus. RESULTS: A pronounced "inland-high-incidence vs. coastal-high-fatality" pattern of SFTS was identified. The incidence of SFTS exhibited divergent sensitivities to meteorological factors; inland transmission was sensitive to thermal fluctuations, whereas coastal dynamics were constrained by a sunshine threshold (> 200 h/month). In contrast, spatial divergence in clinical severity correlated with the distribution of regional viral genetic structures. Inland regions mainly co-circulated genotypes A, C, and D, while coastal regions were dominated by genotype B. Zhejiang province was identified as a genetic hub with significantly higher recombination frequencies than inland regions (11.0% vs. Bayesian phylogeographic inference indicated frequent lineage exchange of Zhejiang province in China with the Republic of Korea and Japan. Clinically, genotypes B and D were associated with elevated mortality in coastal and inland regions, respectively, suggesting that the severe coastal phenotype is shaped by its genotype B-dominated structure. Additionally, the RdRp-N828S mutation emerged as a robust molecular correlate of fatal outcomes, warranting further functional validation. CONCLUSIONS: Divergent meteorological factors and plausible maritime transmission networks may underlie the geographically decoupled epidemiology of SFTS. These findings highlight that risk assessment must extend beyond incidence alone and provide a phylogeographically informed framework for targeted surveillance and genotype-specific interventions in high-risk hotspots.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在阐明东亚地区地理上脱钩的 发病率 和严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 的死亡模式背后的独特生态驱动因素和系统地理学动态。发热伴血小板减少综合征 是由大别班达病毒 (SFTSV) 引起的,在内陆和沿海地区表现出不同的 发病率 和死亡率。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生态模型、贝叶斯系统发育地理学和基因型-表型关联分析,将 1820 个高质量的全球 SFTSV 队列研究 数据与中国的临床 队列研究(936 例患者)和全国 监测 数据(27,457 例)进行整合。
elements_zh.methods: 使用生态模型、贝叶斯系统发育地理学和基因型-表型关联分析来追踪 SFTSV 的进化轨迹和临床意义。该研究利用了来自中国的充分表征的临床 队列研究 和全国 监测 数据。
elements_zh.main_results: 确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的明显“内陆高死亡率 发病率 与沿海高死亡率”模式。发热伴血小板减少综合征的发病率对气象因素表现出不同的敏感性,内陆传播对热波动和受日照阈值(> 200小时/月)限制的沿海动态敏感。临床严重程度的空间差异与区域病毒遗传结构的分布相关,内陆地区以A、C、D基因型共循环为主,沿海地区以B基因型为主。浙江省被确定为遗传中心,其重组频率明显高于内陆地区。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,风险评估必须超越仅 发病率 的范畴,并为高风险热点地区的针对性 发病率 和基因型特异性干预措施提供系统地理学框架。该研究确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 地理解耦 流行病学 背后的不同气象因素和合理的海上 传播 网络。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为高风险热点地区的针对性 监测 和基因型特异性干预措施提供信息,增强对 发热伴血小板减少综合征 流行病学 的理解,并有助于改善公共卫生策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计局限性包括对 监测 数据的依赖以及潜在的抽样偏差。由于该研究的观察性质以及需要对致命结果的分子相关性进行进一步的功能验证,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在阐明东亚地区地理上脱钩的 发病率 和严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 的死亡模式背后的独特生态驱动因素和系统地理学动态。发热伴血小板减少综合征 是由大别班达病毒 (SFTSV) 引起的,在内陆和沿海地区表现出不同的 发病率 和死亡率。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用生态模型、贝叶斯系统发育地理学和基因型-表型关联分析,将 1820 个高质量的全球 SFTSV 队列研究 数据与中国的临床 队列研究(936 例患者)和全国 监测 数据(27,457 例)进行整合。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用生态模型、贝叶斯系统发育地理学和基因型-表型关联分析来追踪 SFTSV 的进化轨迹和临床意义。该研究利用了来自中国的充分表征的临床 队列研究 和全国 监测 数据。
analysis_zh.main_results: 确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 的明显“内陆高死亡率 发病率 与沿海高死亡率”模式。发热伴血小板减少综合征的发病率对气象因素表现出不同的敏感性,内陆传播对热波动和受日照阈值(> 200小时/月)限制的沿海动态敏感。临床严重程度的空间差异与区域病毒遗传结构的分布相关,内陆地区以A、C、D基因型共循环为主,沿海地区以B基因型为主。浙江省被确定为遗传中心,其重组频率明显高于内陆地区。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,风险评估必须超越仅 发病率 的范畴,并为高风险热点地区的针对性 发病率 和基因型特异性干预措施提供系统地理学框架。该研究确定了 发热伴血小板减少综合征 地理解耦 流行病学 背后的不同气象因素和合理的海上 传播 网络。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为高风险热点地区的针对性 监测 和基因型特异性干预措施提供信息,增强对 发热伴血小板减少综合征 流行病学 的理解,并有助于改善公共卫生策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的设计局限性包括对 监测 数据的依赖以及潜在的抽样偏差。由于该研究的观察性质以及需要对致命结果的分子相关性进行进一步的功能验证,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Evaluation of new adjuvants in enhancing the immune response to a candidate of Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus vaccine.
papers.abstract: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is an emerging zoonotic disease caused by the tick-borne bunyavirus SFTSV. SFTSV is primarily transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicorn is ticks and can cause a hemorrhagic fever-like illness characterized by high fever, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiorgan failure, with reported case-fatality rates ranging from 10% to over 30%. Despite its growing public health relevance, no licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies are currently available. Here, we evaluated a beta-propiolactone-inactivated SFTSV vaccine candidate based on strain YL1, formulated with benchmark adjuvants (Addavax and Alhydrogel) or experimental innate immune agonists, including Sendai virus-derived defective interfering RNA (SDI), a RIG-I agonist, and imidazoquinoline-poly(ethylene glycol)-cholesterol conjugate (IMDQ-P-C), a TLR7/8 agonist, alone or in combination. Using an extended prime-boost regimen, we examined adjuvant-dependent modulation of humoral immunity, antigen-specific cellular recall, antibody cross-reactivity, and functional protection following passive serum transfer and live-virus challenge in IFNAR-/- mice. All adjuvanted formulations induced detectable humoral responses, with Addavax and SDI eliciting the highest virus-specific binding and neutralizing antibody titers. Antigen-specific analyses identified the nucleoprotein (NP) as the dominant target of vaccine-induced immune memory. NP elicited robust antibody response and the broadest cytokine recall profile following ex vivo stimulation. This response was broader than that induced by the whole inactivated virus and was characterized by mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across adjuvant formulations. In contrast, the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited cellular recall responses, consistent with its relatively weak humoral immunogenicity after both priming and boosting. Nevertheless, sera from SDI and Addavax-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with Gn from a heterologous SFTSV strain, suggesting broader antibody recognition across viral genotypes. Functionally, sera from SDI and Addavax-immunized mice conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- recipients, as reflected by reduced viral loads, delayed disease onset, and prolonged survival after lethal SFTSV challenge. Together, these findings support the immunogenicity and protective potential of a BPL-inactivated SFTSV vaccine platform and identify NP as a major target of vaccine-induced immune memory. They further highlight the importance of adjuvant selection in shaping the magnitude, antigenic focus, and functional quality of vaccine-induced antiviral immunity. In brief Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne bunyavirus that causes a hemorrhagic fever-like illness with high fatality rates and lacks approved vaccines. Here, we developed and characterized a β-propiolactone-inactivated whole-virus SFTSV vaccine candidate formulated with benchmark and experimental adjuvants, including the RIG-I agonist SDI and the TLR7/8 agonist IMDQ-P-C. In BALB/c mice, Addavax and SDI elicited the strongest virus-specific binding and neutralizing antibody responses. Antigen-specific recall analyses identified nucleoprotein (NP) as the dominant target of vaccine-induced immune memory, eliciting robust antibody responses and the broadest cytokine recall profile after ex vivo stimulation. NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses. Sera from Addavax- and SDI-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with the Gn glycoprotein of the heterologous HB29 strain and conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- mice challenged with live SFTSV. These findings identify NP as a major immunological target of this inactivated vaccine platform and highlight how adjuvant selection shapes the magnitude, antigenic focus, and functional quality of antiviral immunity.

Despite its growing public health relevance, no licensed vaccines or specific antiviral therapies are currently available. Here, we evaluated a beta-propiolactone-inactivated SFTSV vaccine candidate based on strain YL1, formulated with benchmark adjuvants (Addavax and Alhydrogel) or experimental innate immune agonists, including Sendai virus-derived defective interfering RNA (SDI), a RIG-I agonist, and imidazoquinoline-poly(ethylene glycol)-cholesterol conjugate (IMDQ-P-C), a TLR7/8 agonist, alone or in combination. Using an extended prime-boost regimen, we examined adjuvant-dependent modulation of humoral immunity, antigen-specific cellular recall, antibody cross-reactivity, and functional protection following passive serum transfer and live-virus challenge in IFNAR-/- mice. All adjuvanted formulations induced detectable humoral responses, with Addavax and SDI eliciting the highest virus-specific binding and neutralizing antibody titers. Antigen-specific analyses identified the nucleoprotein (NP) as the dominant target of vaccine-induced immune memory. NP elicited robust antibody response and the broadest cytokine recall profile following ex vivo stimulation. This response was broader than that induced by the whole inactivated virus and was characterized by mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across adjuvant formulations. In contrast, the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited cellular recall responses, consistent with its relatively weak humoral immunogenicity after both priming and boosting. Nevertheless, sera from SDI and Addavax-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with Gn from a heterologous SFTSV strain, suggesting broader antibody recognition across viral genotypes. Functionally, sera from SDI and Addavax-immunized mice conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- recipients, as reflected by reduced viral loads, delayed disease onset, and prolonged survival after lethal SFTSV challenge. Together, these findings support the immunogenicity and protective potential of a BPL-inactivated SFTSV vaccine platform and identify NP as a major target of vaccine-induced immune memory. They further highlight the importance of adjuvant selection in shaping the magnitude, antigenic focus, and functional quality of vaccine-induced antiviral immunity. In brief Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne bunyavirus that causes a hemorrhagic fever-like illness with high fatality rates and lacks approved vaccines. Here, we developed and characterized a β-propiolactone-inactivated whole-virus SFTSV vaccine candidate formulated with benchmark and experimental adjuvants, including the RIG-I agonist SDI and the TLR7/8 agonist IMDQ-P-C. In BALB/c mice, Addavax and SDI elicited the strongest virus-specific binding and neutralizing antibody responses. Antigen-specific recall analyses identified nucleoprotein (NP) as the dominant target of vaccine-induced immune memory, eliciting robust antibody responses and the broadest cytokine recall profile after ex vivo stimulation. NP-induced recall showed mixed Th1-associated, Th2-associated, and proinflammatory-associated features that varied across vaccine formulations, whereas the head domain of the Gn glycoprotein elicited limited humoral and cellular responses. Sera from Addavax- and SDI-adjuvanted groups displayed cross-reactivity with the Gn glycoprotein of the heterologous HB29 strain and conferred partial protection following passive transfer into IFNAR-/- mice challenged with live SFTSV. These findings identify NP as a major immunological target of this inactivated vaccine platform and highlight how adjuvant selection shapes the magnitude, antigenic focus, and functional quality of antiviral immunity.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在这里,我们评估了基于菌株 YL1 的 β-丙内酯灭活 SFTSV 疫苗 候选药物,该候选药物采用基准佐剂(Addavax 和 AlHydrogel)或实验性先天免疫激动剂配制而成,包括仙台病毒衍生的缺陷干扰 RNA (SDI)、RIG-I 激动剂和咪唑喹啉-聚乙二醇-胆固醇缀合物 (IMDQ-P-C),TLR7/8 激动剂,单独或组合。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总之,这些发现支持 BPL 灭活的 SFTSV 疫苗 平台的免疫原性和保护潜力,并将 NP 确定为 疫苗 诱导的免疫记忆的主要目标。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 尽管其与公共卫生的相关性日益增强,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 疗法。

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要发热伴血小板减少综合征(发热伴血小板减少综合征)是一种新兴的人兽共患病,由蜱媒布尼亚病毒SFTSV引起。SFTSV主要通过长角血蜱传播,可导致类似出血热的疾病,特征为高热、血小板减少、白细胞减少和多器官功能衰竭,报告的病死率范围从10%到超过30%。尽管其公共卫生相关性日益增加,但目前尚无获批的疫苗或特异性抗病毒药物治疗方法。在此,我们评估了基于YL1株的β-丙烯基内酯灭活SFTSV 疫苗候选疫苗,该疫苗使用基准佐剂(Addavax和Alhydrogel)或实验性固有免疫激动剂,包括来自Sendai病毒的缺陷干扰RNA(SDI)、RIG-I激动剂和咪唑喹啉-聚乙二醇-胆固醇偶联物(IMDQ-P-C)、TLR7/8激动剂,单独或联合使用。通过扩展的初免-加强方案,我们研究了佐剂依赖性对体液免疫、抗原特异性细胞回忆、抗体交叉反应性和功能保护的影响,这些研究在IFNAR-/-小鼠中通过被动血清转移和活病毒挑战进行。所有佐剂配方均诱导可检测到的体液反应,Addavax和SDI诱导的病毒特异性结合和中和抗体滴度最高。抗原特异性分析表明,核蛋白(NP)是疫苗诱导免疫记忆的主要靶标。NP诱导的抗体反应和体外刺激后的最广泛的细胞因子回忆谱最为强烈。这种反应比整个灭活病毒诱导的更广泛,具有混合的Th1相关、Th2相关和促炎相关特征,这些特征在不同佐剂配方中有所不同。相比之下,Gn糖蛋白的头部域诱导了有限的细胞回忆反应,这与其在初次免疫和加强免疫后的较弱体液免疫原性一致。然而,SDI和Addavax佐剂组的血清与异源HB29株的Gn糖蛋白显示出交叉反应性,表明疫苗诱导的抗体识别范围更广。功能上,SDI和Addavax免疫的小鼠血清在IFNAR-/-受体中被动转移后部分保护了小鼠,表现为病毒载量降低、疾病发作延迟和存活时间延长。这些发现支持了β-丙烯基内酯灭活SFTSV 疫苗平台的免疫原性和保护潜力,并确定了NP作为疫苗诱导免疫记忆的主要靶标。它们进一步强调了佐剂选择在塑造疫苗诱导的抗病毒药物免疫的强度、抗原焦点和功能质量方面的重要性。简而言之,发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱媒布尼亚病毒,可引起类似出血热的疾病,病死率高,目前尚无获批的疫苗。在此,我们开发并表征了基于基准和实验性佐剂的β-丙烯基内酯灭活全病毒SFTSV 疫苗候选疫苗,包括RIG-I激动剂SDI和TLR7/8激动剂IMDQ-P-C。在BALB/c小鼠中,Addavax和SDI诱导了最强的病毒特异性结合和中和抗体反应。抗原特异性回忆分析表明,核蛋白(NP)是疫苗诱导免疫记忆的主要靶标,在体外刺激后诱导了最广泛的细胞因子回忆谱。NP诱导的回忆反应具有混合的Th1相关、Th2相关和促炎相关特征,这些特征在不同疫苗配方中有所不同,而Gn糖蛋白的头部域仅诱导了有限的体液和细胞反应。Addavax和SDI佐剂组的血清与异源HB29株的Gn糖蛋白显示出交叉反应性,并在IFNAR-/-小鼠中被动转移后部分保护了小鼠免受活SFTSV的挑战。这些发现确定了NP作为这种灭活疫苗平台的主要免疫学靶标,并突显了佐剂选择如何塑造抗病毒药物免疫的强度、抗原焦点和功能质量。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 在这里,我们评估了基于菌株 YL1 的 β-丙内酯灭活 SFTSV 疫苗 候选药物,该候选药物采用基准佐剂(Addavax 和 AlHydrogel)或实验性先天免疫激动剂配制而成,包括仙台病毒衍生的缺陷干扰 RNA (SDI)、RIG-I 激动剂和咪唑喹啉-聚乙二醇-胆固醇缀合物 (IMDQ-P-C),TLR7/8 激动剂,单独或组合。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: SFTSV 主要由长角血蜱传播,可引起出血热样疾病,其特征为高烧、血小板减少、白细胞减少和多器官衰竭,报告的病死率从 10% 到 30% 以上。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用延长的初免-加强方案,我们检查了 IFNAR-/- 小鼠被动血清转移和活病毒攻击后的体液免疫、抗原特异性细胞召回、抗体交叉反应性和功能保护的佐剂依赖性调节。
analysis_zh.main_results: NP 诱导的回忆显示出混合的 Th1 相关、Th2 相关和促炎相关特征,这些特征在 疫苗 制剂中各不相同,而 Gn 糖蛋白的头域引起有限的体液和细胞反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总之,这些发现支持 BPL 灭活的 SFTSV 疫苗 平台的免疫原性和保护潜力,并将 NP 确定为 疫苗 诱导的免疫记忆的主要目标。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 尽管其与公共卫生的相关性日益增强,但目前尚无获得许可的 疫苗 或特定的 抗病毒药物 疗法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 来自 Addavax 和 SDI 佐剂组的血清表现出与异源 HB29 菌株的 Gn 糖蛋白的交叉反应性,并在被动转移到用活 SFTSV 攻击的 IFNAR-/- 小鼠中后提供部分保护。

papers.title: Establishment and application of a multiplex qPCR panel for multi-host surveillance of tick-Borne pathogens.
papers.abstract: Tick-borne diseases pose significant public health threats. Non-specific symptoms and co-infections present diagnostic challenges for conventional methods. To address this, we developed the tick-borne pathogen (TBP) Panel, utilizing eight separate multiplex qPCR assays to simultaneously detect 25 TBPs (7 bacteria, 14 viruses, 4 parasites). Optimal Quantification Cycle (Cq) cut-offs were established using nested/semi-nested PCR amplicon sequencing, and digital PCR as reference standards. The Panel was then deployed for screening 2,333 ticks, 59 rodents, and 553 febrile patients. The Panel demonstrated robust analytical performance, achieving limits of detection (LOD 99% ) being 3.5-131 copies/reaction of plasmid, 10 2 -10 3 copies/mL of blood and 10 3 -10 4 copies/tick pool. This study established a tiered determination framework (Cq ≤ 36.6 as positive; Cq 36.6-39.6 requiring dual-replicate confirmation), yielding an overall AUC of 0.979, with 96.5% sensitivity and 96.5% specificity. Screening revealed a diverse pathogen landscape, identifying a total of 14 pathogens in 16.9% of the ticks (395/2,333), revealing a diverse geographical distribution. Five pathogens were identified in 7.9% of AFI patients (25/317), including Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV) and Ehrlichia spp., which were found circulating in local ticks. In the FUO cohort, a single case of Rickettsia spp. Rodent surveillance identified four pathogens, predominantly Bartonella spp. In conclusion , the rigorously validated TBP Panel enables rapid etiological identification of undifferentiated febrile illnesses, serving as a high-throughput tool that bridges large-scale surveillance with clinical diagnostics to close critical gaps in tick-borne disease management.

source_records.title: Establishment and application of a multiplex qPCR panel for multi-host surveillance of tick-Borne pathogens
source_records.abstract: Tick-borne diseases pose significant public health threats. Non-specific symptoms and co-infections present diagnostic challenges for conventional methods. To address this, we developed the tick-borne pathogen (TBP) Panel, utilizing eight separate multiplex qPCR assays to simultaneously detect 25 TBPs (7 bacteria, 14 viruses, 4 parasites). Optimal Quantification Cycle (Cq) cut-offs were established using nested/semi-nested PCR amplicon sequencing, and digital PCR as reference standards. The Panel was then deployed for screening 2,333 ticks, 59 rodents, and 553 febrile patients. The Panel demonstrated robust analytical performance, achieving limits of detection (LOD99%) being 3.5–131 copies/reaction of plasmid, 102–103 copies/mL of blood and 103–104 copies/tick pool. This study established a tiered determination framework (Cq ≤ 36.6 as positive; Cq 36.6–39.6 requiring dual-replicate confirmation), yielding an overall AUC of 0.979, with 96.5% sensitivity and 96.5% specificity. Screening revealed a diverse pathogen landscape, identifying a total of 14 pathogens in 16.9% of the ticks (395/2,333), revealing a diverse geographical distribution. Five pathogens were identified in 7.9% of AFI patients (25/317), including Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Virus (SFTSV) and Ehrlichia spp., which were found circulating in local ticks. In the FUO cohort, a single case of Rickettsia spp. Rodent surveillance identified four pathogens, predominantly Bartonella spp. In conclusion , the rigorously validated TBP Panel enables rapid etiological identification of undifferentiated febrile illnesses, serving as a high-throughput tool that bridges large-scale surveillance with clinical diagnostics to close critical gaps in tick-borne disease management.

papers.abstract_zh: 蜱媒 疾病对公共卫生构成重大威胁。非特异性症状和合并感染给传统方法的诊断带来了挑战。为了解决这个问题,我们开发了 蜱媒 病原体 (TBP) 组合,利用八种独立的多重 qPCR 检测同时检测 25 种 TBP(7 种细菌、14 种病毒、4 种寄生虫)。使用巢式/半巢式 PCR 扩增子测序和数字 PCR 作为参考标准,建立了最佳定量循环 (Cq) 截止值。该小组随后被部署对 2,333 只蜱虫、59 只啮齿动物和 553 名发热患者进行筛查。该小组展示了强大的分析性能,检测限 (LOD 99%) 为 3.5-131 拷贝/质粒反应、10 2 -10 3 拷贝/mL 血液和 10 3 -10 4 拷贝/蜱池。本研究建立了分级判定框架(Cq≤36.6为阳性;Cq 36.6-39.6需要双重复确认),总体AUC为0.979,敏感性为96.5%,特异性为96.5%。筛查揭示了多样化的病原体景观,在 16.9% 的蜱虫中总共鉴定出 14 种病原体 (395/2,333),揭示了多样化的地理分布。7.9% 的 AFI 患者 (25/317) 中发现了五种病原体,包括 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 和埃利希体属,这些病原体在当地蜱中传播。在 FUO 队列研究 中,发现一例立克次体属。啮齿动物 监测 鉴定出四种病原体,主要是巴尔通体属。总之,经过严格验证的 TBP Panel 能够快速识别未分化发热性疾病的病因,作为一种高通量工具,将大规模 监测 与临床诊断联系起来,以缩小 蜱媒 疾病管理中的关键差距。

papers.title: Multidimensional mechanisms of SFTSV-host interactions: viral protein functions, m6A modification, tick saliva factors, and platelet regulation
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), officially designated as Dabie bandavirus by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses (ICTV), is an emerging zoonotic pathogen belonging to the order Bunyavirales and the family Phenuiviridae. First isolated and identified in 2010 from the serum of patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in China, SFTSV has since been reported in multiple provinces across China, as well as in South Korea, Japan, Vietnam, the United Arab Emirates (including Dubai), and Pakistan. With a case fatality rate of up to 30%, SFTSV poses a serious threat to public health and carries the potential for broader global spread. In nature, SFTSV is primarily transmitted through tick bites, although direct human-to-human or animal-to-human transmission can also occur through exposure to the blood, respiratory secretions, or other bodily fluids of infected individuals or animals. The pathogenic mechanisms of SFTSV are complex and multifaceted, involving the coordinated actions of multiple viral proteins, host epigenetic regulation, and virus–vector interactions. In this review, we take tick bites as the starting point to describe how SFTSV achieves cross-species transmission through ticks, summarize the viral life cycle, including internalization, replication, assembly, and egress, and discuss the antagonistic interplay between the viral life cycle and host defense responses, with the aim of providing a solid theoretical foundation for understanding the infection and pathogenesis of SFTSV.

First isolated and identified in 2010 from the serum of patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) in China, SFTSV has since been reported in multiple provinces across China, as well as in South Korea, Japan, Vietnam, the United Arab Emirates (including Dubai), and Pakistan. With a case fatality rate of up to 30%, SFTSV poses a serious threat to public health and carries the potential for broader global spread. In nature, SFTSV is primarily transmitted through tick bites, although direct human-to-human or animal-to-human transmission can also occur through exposure to the blood, respiratory secretions, or other bodily fluids of infected individuals or animals. The pathogenic mechanisms of SFTSV are complex and multifaceted, involving the coordinated actions of multiple viral proteins, host epigenetic regulation, and virus–vector interactions. In this review, we take tick bites as the starting point to describe how SFTSV achieves cross-species transmission through ticks, summarize the viral life cycle, including internalization, replication, assembly, and egress, and discuss the antagonistic interplay between the viral life cycle and host defense responses, with the aim of providing a solid theoretical foundation for understanding the infection and pathogenesis of SFTSV.
papers.abstract_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 被国际病毒分类委员会 (ICTV) 正式命名为大别班达病毒,是一种新兴的人畜共患病原体,属于布尼亚病毒目、苯鸟病毒科。SFTSV 于 2010 年首次从中国严重发热伴血小板减少综合征 (发热伴血小板减少综合征) 患者的血清中分离和鉴定,此后在中国多个省份以及韩国、日本、越南、阿拉伯联合酋长国(包括迪拜)和巴基斯坦均有报道。SFTSV 病死率高达 30%,对公共健康构成严重威胁,并有可能在全球范围内广泛传播。在自然界中,SFTSV 主要通过蜱虫叮咬传播,但直接人传人或动物传人的 传播 也可能通过接触受感染个体或动物的血液、呼吸道分泌物或其他体液而发生。SFTSV的致病机制复杂且多方面,涉及多种病毒蛋白的协调作用、宿主表观遗传调控以及病毒-媒介相互作用。本文以蜱叮咬为切入点,描述SFTSV如何通过蜱实现跨物种传播,总结病毒生命周期,包括内化、复制、组装和外出,并讨论病毒生命周期与宿主防御反应之间的拮抗相互作用,旨在为理解SFTSV的感染和发病机制提供坚实的理论基础。

papers.title: Neuroactive effects of nootkatone against Haemaphysalis longicornis vectors: AChE inhibition and CYP450-linked metabolic modulation.
papers.abstract: Haemaphysalis longicornis, an ixodid vector associated with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, remains an important target for vector-control. Screening of Alpinia oxyphylla fruit essential oil identified nootkatone as the principal constituent associated with nymphicidal activity. Purified nootkatone showed activity against H. longicornis nymphs, with an LC 50 of 0.058 μg/cm 2 . NTN3 and NTN3 plus piperonyl butoxide (PBO) yielded numerically lower LC 50 values of 0.034 and 0.026 μg/cm 2 , respectively; however, because no formal LC 50 comparison or interaction analysis was performed, these values were interpreted only as descriptive shifts in apparent potency. To characterize exposure-associated biochemical responses, AChE activity, detoxification-related enzyme activities, PBO-associated LC 50 shifts, and molecular docking predictions were examined. In vitro nootkatone exposure reduced acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity by 39.0-80.9% across the tested concentrations, while LC 50 exposure was associated with a 48.0% reduction in AChE activity. These findings indicate an association between nootkatone exposure and reduced AChE activity but do not establish a causal role in mortality. 7-Eethoxycoumarin O-deethylation (ECOD) activity increased by 15.4% after nootkatone exposure, whereas glutathione S-transferase (GST) and α/β-esterase activities were not altered. Because ECOD is a general CYP450-linked proxy assay, this increase indicates altered monooxygenase activity rather than nootkatone-specific detoxification. PBO pre-exposure reduced ECOD activity and was accompanied by numerically lower LC 50 estimates, but these parallel responses alone, without formal mediation analysis, do not demonstrate that ECOD inhibition caused the LC 50 shift. Nootkatone is a promising vector-control candidate against H. longicornis nymphs, although causal mechanisms, environmental safety, and field applicability require further evaluation.

papers.abstract_zh: 长角血蜱(Haemaphysalis longicornis)是一种与严重发热伴血小板减少综合征相关的蜱虫 媒介,仍然是 媒介 控制的重要目标。对益智果精油的筛选鉴定出诺卡酮是与杀螨活性相关的主要成分。纯化的诺卡酮表现出对抗长角长角若虫的活性,LC 50 为0.058 μg/cm 2。NTN3 和 NTN3 加胡椒基丁醚 (PBO) 产生的 LC 50 数值较低,分别为 0.034 和 0.026 μg/cm 2;然而,由于没有进行正式的 LC 50 比较或相互作用分析,这些值仅被解释为表观效力的描述性变化。为了表征与暴露相关的生化反应,检查了 AChE 活性、解毒相关酶活性、PBO 相关 LC 50 变化和分子对接预测。体外诺卡酮暴露在测试浓度范围内使乙酰胆碱酯酶 (AChE) 活性降低了 39.0-80.9%,而 LC 50 暴露与 AChE 活性降低 48.0% 相关。这些发现表明诺卡酮暴露与乙酰胆碱酯酶活性降低之间存在关联,但并未确定 死亡率 中的因果作用。诺卡酮暴露后,7-乙氧基香豆素 O-脱乙基化 (ECOD) 活性增加了 15.4%,而谷胱甘肽 S-转移酶 (GST) 和 α/β-酯酶活性没有改变。由于 ECOD 是一种通用的 CYP450 相关代理检测,因此这种增加表明单加氧酶活性发生改变,而不是诺特卡酮特异性解毒作用。PBO 预暴露降低了 ECOD 活性,并伴随着数值上较低的 LC 50 估计值,但这些平行反应本身(没有正式的中介分析)并不能证明 ECOD 抑制导致 LC 50 变化。Nootkatone 是一种很有前途的 媒介 控制长角若虫的候选药物,尽管其因果机制、环境安全性和现场适用性需要进一步评估。

papers.title: Viral infection activates the IRF1-BAK axis to drive mitochondria-derived inflammation.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria can drive the development of inflammatory pathogenesis through releasing pro-inflammatory DAMPs, a process often triggered during virus infection. Whether a common mechanism exists that promotes virus-triggered mitochondria-derived inflammation is currently unknown. Here, we report that BAK is an interferon-stimulated gene that is up-regulated by the STAT1-IRF1 axis during virus infection to induce mitochondria-derived inflammatory pathogenesis. Viral infection triggers STAT1-dependent up-regulation of IRF1, which binds to an identified ISRE site in the BAK-promoter, inducing BAK up-regulation. Up-regulated BAK accumulates in the mitochondria triggering mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization and inflammatory responses. Both RNA and DNA viruses trigger the IRF1-mediated BAK up-regulation and mitochondria-derived inflammation. Using the Bak-/- mouse model, we showed that both IAV and SFTSV, two viruses that induce severe inflammation in patients, trigger BAK up-regulation and BAK-dependent lethal inflammation. These results reveal a common mechanism that drives mitochondria-derived pathogenic inflammation, which can be targeted for developing anti-inflammatory therapeutics.

Home Health & Wellness Thailand watches deadly tick-borne virus after six SFTS cases Health & Wellness News Pattaya-Thailand Thailand watches deadly tick-borne virus after six SFTS cases By Pattaya Mail September 13, 2026 0 1762 Share on Facebook Tweet on Twitter tweet Health authorities are monitoring SFTS, a tick-borne virus that can cause high fever, low platelets, organ failure and death, after six cases were reported in Thailand. BANGKOK, Thailand – Thailand’s Department of Disease Control is asking health authorities to closely monitor Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), an emerging viral infection that can cause high fever, low platelet counts and potentially fatal complications. The department’s Epidemiology Division said SFTS can begin with sudden high fever, vomiting and diarrhoea before progressing to thrombocytopenia, liver inflammation, shock and multiple-organ failure. Reported fatality rates in affected countries range from 10% to 30%. SFTS is primarily associated with ticks, although transmission from animals to humans and between people through exposure to an infected patient’s blood or bodily fluids has also been reported. The World Health Organization reported that two laboratory-confirmed cases in Phetchabun in June 2025 were associated with close contact with pet dogs, while infected dog ticks were found around the patients’ homes. Thailand first confirmed an SFTS case in 2019. Retrospective testing later identified additional infections in Bangkok and nearby provinces. The latest cases reported in June 2025 brought the number of identified cases cited by Thai health authorities to six, with cases reported in Bangkok, Phetchabun, Nakhon Pathom and Chachoengsao. The department said Thailand has several factors that could allow further infections, including environments suitable for ticks, close contact with pets that may carry ticks, the importation of animals that could harbour ticks and travel to areas where SFTS is circulating. The tick of concern can feed on a wide range of animals, including cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, horses, pigs, dogs, cats, wild animals and rodents. It can also bite humans. Thai authorities have previously found the relevant tick species during surveys in some national parks, although there has not been conclusive evidence establishing that the tick has become permanently established in Thailand. The Department of Disease Control has therefore asked provincial health offices, the Bangkok health authorities and disease-control units to strengthen surveillance and follow developments involving SFTS. Health officials have also highlighted the importance of considering SFTS in patients with fever and low platelet counts, particularly when there is a history of tick exposure. A 2026 study has provided further evidence linking SFTS infections in Thailand with Rhipicephalus sanguineus, commonly known as the brown dog tick. Researchers detected the virus in ticks collected from dogs and the environment associated with two fatal human infections, adding to concerns about dog-associated tick transmission. Authorities are continuing to monitor the situation while urging greater awareness among health workers and the public, particularly where people have close contact with animals that may carry ticks. news.content: Close Menu Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Biology Chemistry Earth Health Physics Science Space Technology Facebook X (Twitter) Pinterest YouTube RSS Home»Health»New Tick-Borne Virus May Explain Mysterious Cases of Severe Illness Health New Tick-Borne Virus May Explain Mysterious Cases of Severe Illness By Mary Van Beusekom, University of MinnesotaSeptember 12, 2026No Comments4 Mins Read Facebook Twitter Pinterest Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Email Reddit Share Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Pinterest Telegram Email Reddit Ticks are small blood-feeding arachnids that can carry a wide range of viruses, bacteria, and parasites. Because different pathogens can circulate in the same tick species, the illnesses they cause may overlap and be difficult to distinguish. Credit: Stock Some unexplained cases of severe tick-related illness may have a previously overlooked cause. A newly identified tick-borne virus may help explain why some patients in China develop symptoms resembling a dangerous hemorrhagic fever even though tests for the expected virus come back negative. Researchers identified the virus as Asian longhorned tick nairovirus, or ALTNV. Among 3,163 patients tested in areas where tick-borne viruses circulate, 10.4% showed evidence of ALTNV infection. Among patients who tested negative for Dabie bandavirus, or DBV, 15.1% tested positive for ALTNV. DBV causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, a tick-borne disease found across Asia. Thrombocytopenia means a person has an abnormally low number of platelets, the blood cells that help with clotting. The disease has a reported fatality rate of 10% to 30%, and the World Health Organization lists DBV as a priority for research. Negative DBV tests reveal another virus Yet about 30% of patients with signs and symptoms suggesting DBV infection test negative for the virus. That unexplained group prompted researchers led by the State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity in Beijing to search for another possible cause. The team collected samples from people who had been bitten by ticks and sought care at sentinel hospitals in parts of China where tick-borne viruses circulate. Using RNA sequencing and viral isolation, they identified ALTNV and determined that it belongs to a group of viruses known as orthonairoviruses within the Nairoviridae family. Genetic analysis showed that ALTNV shared less than 80% amino acid similarity with other species in the same genus, supporting its identification as a distinct virus. The researchers then tested whether ALTNV could reproduce in the laboratory. Serum from patients that contained ALTNV RNA produced viral growth in cultured cells. Immunofluorescence testing detected ALTNV viral antigens, while electron microscopy revealed features characteristic of orthonairoviruses. The virus was also able to replicate in several types of cells. Coinfection brought more severe outcomes The illnesses seen in patients differed depending on whether ALTNV occurred alone or together with DBV. Among patients infected only with ALTNV, fatigue was the most common symptom, affecting 84%. Because different pathogens can circulate in the same tick species, the illnesses they cause may overlap and be difficult to distinguish. Credit: Stock Some unexplained cases of severe tick-related illness may have a previously overlooked cause. A newly identified tick-borne virus may help explain why some patients in China develop symptoms resembling a dangerous hemorrhagic fever even though tests for the expected virus come back negative. Among patients who tested negative for Dabie bandavirus, or DBV, 15.1% tested positive for ALTNV. DBV causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, a tick-borne disease found across Asia. Thrombocytopenia means a person has an abnormally low number of platelets, the blood cells that help with clotting. The disease has a reported fatality rate of 10% to 30%, and the World Health Organization lists DBV as a priority for research. Genetic analysis showed that ALTNV shared less than 80% amino acid similarity with other species in the same genus, supporting its identification as a distinct virus. The researchers then tested whether ALTNV could reproduce in the laboratory. Serum from patients that contained ALTNV RNA produced viral growth in cultured cells. The virus was also able to replicate in several types of cells. Kidney impairment occurred in 84% of coinfected patients, compared with 66% of those with DBV alone. Seven of the 38 patients with both viruses died, representing 18.4% of the coinfected group. Asian longhorned ticks carried ALTNV The researchers also investigated how widely ALTNV was circulating among ticks. They detected ALTNV RNA in 1.3% of 47,428 ticks collected across 15 Chinese provinces. The Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, had the highest prevalence, with 1.8% testing positive. Laboratory experiments also showed that this tick species could transmit ALTNV to mice, providing evidence that it can carry and spread the virus. A shared tick complicates diagnosis That overlap could complicate diagnosis. ALTNV and DBV circulate in the same regions, share a tick vector, and can produce overlapping symptoms, making it difficult to determine which infection a patient has based on symptoms alone. “The cocirculation of ALTNV and DBV in the same areas, coupled with their shared tick vector, underscores the need for improved differential diagnosis between infections with these viruses in regions where SFTS is endemic,” the authors concluded. news.content: Skip to content Home Topics Brain & Mental Health Cancer Care & Research Children’s Health Diseases & Conditions Heart and Vascular Health Health & Wellness Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Spine Care Trauma Women's Health Podcasts Find a Doctor Search Home Topics Brain & Mental Health Cancer Care & Research Children’s Health Diseases & Conditions Heart and Vascular Health Health & Wellness Orthopedics & Sports Medicine Spine Care Trauma Women's Health Podcasts Find a Doctor Search Search FacebookXEmailLinkedIn Infectious Diseases New Tick-Borne Virus Called a Nairovirus: What to Know About ALTNV September 11, 2026 5 min read Scientists in China have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that can cause a flu-like illness. The virus, called Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), was identified in patients who had been bitten by ticks and developed symptoms including fever, fatigue and gastrointestinal problems. The discovery, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, is another reminder of how much scientists continue to learn about the viruses and other germs that ticks can carry. What Is ALTNV? ALTNV is a newly identified virus in the orthonairovirus group. Researchers discovered it while investigating patients in China who had been bitten by ticks and developed fever and other symptoms but who were negative for all currently known viruses. The researchers tested 3,163 patients and found evidence of ALTNV infection in about 10 percent of them. Among the patients who had ALTNV alone, the most common symptoms included fatigue, digestive problems, fever and low platelet counts, also known as thrombocytopenia. All 56 patients with ALTNV alone recovered. Some patients were infected with both ALTNV and Dabie bandavirus (DBV), the virus that causes severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS (an illness unique to China). Seven of the 38 patients with both infections died. The researchers found that people with both viruses tended to have more severe illness than those infected with ALTNV alone. What Is SFTS? Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, or SFTS, is a serious illness caused by Dabie bandavirus. This illness is not associated with any other ticks except the Asian Long Horned tick. This illness is only found in China. The name describes two of its main features: a high fever and a low platelet count. Platelets are blood cells that help the body form clots. SFTS can cause serious complications and can be fatal. Reported fatality rates in areas where the disease occurs have been about 10 percent to 30 percent. Importantly, that mortality rate refers to SFTS caused by Dabie bandavirus, not ALTNV alone. In the new study, all patients who had ALTNV alone recovered. The deaths occurred among patients who were infected with both ALTNV and Dabie bandavirus. What Does This Mean for the United States? There is currently no evidence that ALTNV is causing human illness in the United States. The virus was identified in patients in China. This is important information for travelers, those going to China and those returning from trips to China. Please inform your medical provider of your itinerary as these details will help them to deliver the best care to you. However, the tick associated with ALTNV, the Asian longhorned tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis), is already present in parts of the United States, including New York. The presence of the tick does not mean that ALTNV is circulating here. The United States has many other tick-borne diseases to be aware of. In New York, these include: Lyme Disease Anaplasmosis Ehrlichiosis Babesiosis Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever Bourbon Virus STARI Alpha-Gal Syndrome Ticks Carry Many Different Germs One important takeaway from this discovery is that ticks can carry many different viruses, bacteria and parasites, and scientists continue to improve their ability to identify them. Many tick-borne illnesses can cause similar symptoms, such as fever, fatigue, headache and muscle aches. Understanding which infections are present in a particular region, along with a person’s history of tick exposure, can help healthcare providers determine what testing and treatment may be appropriate. How to Protect Yourself From Tick Bites The best way to prevent tick-borne illness is to prevent tick bites. When spending time outdoors: Use tick repellent. Follow the product directions and choose a repellent appropriate for your age and activity. Cover up. Wear long pants and consider tucking pants into socks when walking through areas where ticks may be present. Check for ticks. Check yourself and your children after spending time outdoors. Look carefully around the scalp and hairline, behind the ears and knees, around the waist and in other areas where ticks can hide. Check pets, too. Dogs and other pets can carry ticks into the home. Remove ticks promptly. If you find an attached tick, remove it as soon as possible with fine-tipped tweezers. If you develop a fever, unusual fatigue, rash or other symptoms after a tick bite or spending time in an area where ticks are common, contact your healthcare provider. Many tick-borne illnesses can look similar to one another in the early stages, so your symptoms and recent exposure are important information for your physician. The Bottom Line The discovery of ALTNV does not mean this virus is circulating in the United States. It does show that scientists are continuing to discover new germs carried by ticks and improve the ways they identify them. For families, the advice remains simple: prevent tick bites, check for ticks after spending time outdoors and remove attached ticks promptly. Sharon Nachman, MD Pediatric Infectious Diseases Dr. Sharon Nachman is a board-certified pediatric infectious disease specialist with more than 30 years of experience caring for infants, children, and adolescents. She is internationally recognized for her research in pediatric infectious diseases and serves as Principal Investigator and Chair of the NIH-funded International Maternal Pediatric Adolescent AIDS Clinical Trials Network (IMPAACT). Dr. Nachman has led clinical trials that have advanced treatments for HIV, tuberculosis, vaccines, and new therapies for children. She also specializes in caring for children with common and complex infections, including resistant bacterial and tick-borne infections. news.content_title: Gyeonggi Province Urges Caution Against Tick-borne Diseases During Farm Work and Outdoor Activities - The Asia Business Daily
news.content: container The Asia Business Daily Open Navigation Stock Economy Real estate Industry · IT Politics Society World Culture·Life Opinion·Editorial Visual-News Society Gyeonggi Province Urges Caution Against Tick-borne Diseases During Farm Work and Outdoor Activities Language Language Close KR CN Open Search bar Search field News Search Remove icon Search icon Dim Society Region Gyeonggi Province Urges Caution Against Tick-borne Diseases During Farm Work and Outdoor Activities by Lee YeongKyu Published 14 Sep.2026 07:24(KST) Share Language Text Size Print Gyeonggi Province has urged residents to follow tick-borne disease prevention guidelines as outdoor activities such as rice paddy and field work, mowing grass, harvesting, visiting ancestral graves, and hiking increase during this season. The Gyeonggi Institute of Health and Environment announced on September 14 that tick-borne diseases such as Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS), Tsutsugamushi disease, and Lyme disease occur most frequently between April and November, when farming and outdoor activities are most active. Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) is a Class 3 nationally notifiable infectious disease transmitted through bites from ticks that carry the virus. After an incubation period of 5 to 14 days, symptoms such as high fever, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pain, and chills may appear. If the disease progresses to a severe state, it can lead to thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, and multiple organ failure. Currently, there is no preventive vaccine or treatment, so prevention is especially important. The provincial Institute of Health and Environment tested 204 suspected SFTS cases from January to August of this year, with 12 cases testing positive, resulting in a positive rate of 5.9%. Although the number of tests decreased by 10.5% compared to the same period last year, the number of confirmed cases increased from 10 to 12. Among positive cases, those aged 50 and older made up 75% (9 people), which means extra caution is required for middle-aged and elderly individuals during farm work and outdoor activities. Tick-Borne Disease Prevention Guidelines Poster View original image When engaging in outdoor activities, it is recommended to wear long sleeves, long pants, gloves, and socks to minimize skin exposure, and to use tick repellents. Do not leave clothes on grass or lie down in grassy areas, and use designated trails when hiking. After finishing outdoor work or activities, wash your clothes immediately and shower, carefully checking areas where ticks could attach, such as around the hair, ears, armpits, waist, and behind the knees. If you find a tick attached to your body, avoid crushing it with your hands; instead, remove it with tweezers and visit a medical facility for treatment. Furthermore, if you develop suspected symptoms within two weeks after outdoor activities, inform your healthcare provider about any recent farm work or outdoor activities and seek medical attention immediately. The Gyeonggi Provincial Agricultural Research and Extension Services distributed 1,830 promotional leaflets and 1,680 tick repellents since April to provide preventive education to the province’s farmers, who are frequently outdoors during the farming season. In addition, they continue to provide ongoing guidance about prevention through farm safety managers and heat stroke prevention officers. Kim Myungkil, Head of the Infectious Disease Research Division at the Provincial Institute of Health and Environment, said, "Not everyone bitten by a tick becomes infected, as only a small proportion of ticks carry the virus. Rather than excessive anxiety, it is important to strictly follow prevention guidelines. In the autumn, there are many opportunities to come into contact with ticks—not only during farm work but also while mowing grass, visiting ancestral graves, and hiking—so please make sure to practice preventive measures before and after any outdoor activity." Knowridge Science Report Home Science Biology Chemistry Physics Tech Energy Computer Science Engineering Health Nutrition Wellness Medicine Mind Mental Health Neuroscience Psychology Earth Space Home Medicine New Tick Virus Found in China Medicine Public Health New Tick Virus Found in China By Knowridge - September 16, 2026 Credit: CDC/Unsplash. Scientists in China have identified a previously unknown virus carried by ticks that can make people sick with fever, tiredness and stomach problems. The discovery may help explain why some patients who appear to have a known tick-borne disease repeatedly test negative for it. The new virus has been named Asian longhorned tick nairovirus, or ALTNV. Researchers led by scientists at the State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity in Beijing reported the discovery in the New England Journal of Medicine. Their work suggests the virus is circulating across a surprisingly wide area of China. Ticks are small parasites that feed on the blood of animals and people. During feeding, some species can pass viruses, bacteria and other disease-causing organisms into the bloodstream. Tick-borne diseases are a growing public health concern in many parts of the world. The researchers began investigating patients with symptoms similar to severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, often shortened to SFTS. This serious illness is caused by Dabie bandavirus, or DBV, and occurs in several Asian countries. It can cause high fever, extreme tiredness and dangerously low levels of platelets, the blood cells that help stop bleeding. DBV infection can be severe, with previous estimates suggesting that roughly 10% to 30% of diagnosed patients may die. Yet doctors had noticed a puzzle. About 30% of patients with signs that looked like the disease tested negative for the virus, raising the possibility that another infection was producing similar symptoms. To investigate, scientists collected samples from people who had experienced tick bites and were treated at hospitals in areas where tick-borne viruses are common. They examined genetic material in the samples and isolated the newly discovered virus. Further laboratory work confirmed that ALTNV could reproduce inside several types of cells. The scale of the testing was substantial. Among 3,163 patients examined, 10.4% showed evidence of ALTNV infection based on either viral genetic material or antibodies produced by the immune system. Among patients who had tested negative for DBV, 15.1% showed evidence of the new virus. People infected only with ALTNV commonly experienced fatigue, which affected 84% of cases. About 80% developed digestive problems, while 38% had low platelet levels. Around 36% had higher levels of certain enzymes in their blood that can rise when the liver or other tissues are irritated or injured. Encouragingly, the patients identified as having ALTNV alone recovered completely in this study. That does not yet establish how dangerous the virus may be in every group of people, however. Newly discovered infections often require years of monitoring before scientists understand their full range of symptoms and risks. The researchers also found people infected with both ALTNV and DBV at the same time. There were 38 such patients, and their illnesses appeared more serious in some respects than infections involving DBV alone. Respiratory symptoms and signs of kidney problems were more common in the patients with both viruses. Seven of the 38 people with both infections died, representing 18.4% of that group. The study cannot by itself prove that ALTNV made the DBV infections more deadly, because the number of coinfected patients was small and other differences could have affected their outcomes. Still, the finding gives researchers an important reason to investigate coinfection more closely. The scientists then looked for the virus in ticks themselves. They tested 47,428 ticks collected from 15 Chinese provinces and detected ALTNV genetic material in about 1.3% of them. The highest rate was found in the Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, at about 1.8%. This tick species is widespread in parts of Asia and has also appeared in other regions of the world. In laboratory experiments, the researchers showed that Asian longhorned ticks could transmit ALTNV to mice. This provides evidence that the tick can act as a carrier of the virus, although transmission patterns in people still need further study. The discovery has practical importance because ALTNV and DBV can circulate in the same places and can be carried by the same tick species. Patients may also develop overlapping symptoms, making it difficult for doctors to know which virus is responsible based on symptoms alone. Better diagnostic tests could help doctors distinguish between the infections. The study is strong because researchers combined patient testing, virus isolation, genetic analysis, laboratory experiments and a very large survey of ticks. Together, these different forms of evidence make a convincing case that ALTNV is a genuine tick-borne virus infecting people. The work also offers a possible explanation for some previously unexplained illnesses that resembled DBV infection. Important questions remain. Researchers need to determine how common ALTNV infection is outside the areas studied, whether it can cause severe disease on its own, which people are most vulnerable and whether other animals help maintain the virus in nature. Scientists will also need to watch for the virus in other countries where Asian longhorned ticks are found. For now, the discovery does not suggest a new global emergency. Instead, it shows how much remains unknown about viruses carried by ticks and why surveillance matters. Identifying ALTNV should make it easier to study unexplained fever after tick bites and could eventually help doctors provide more accurate diagnoses. news.content: Open menu NTD Television U.S.ChinaWorldPoliticsHealthBusinessEntertainmentSports More ●LIVE search EN▼ NTD Television NewsChina News New Tick-Borne Virus Discovered in China Traced to Hundreds of Fever Cases Chinese researchers, working with U.S. collaborators, have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that appears to be responsible for hundreds of previously unexplained fever cases in China. By Sophia Lam | Published: 9/11/2026, 7:44:02 AM EDT An Asian longhorned tick in July 2025. (Griffin Dill/University of Maine via AP) Chinese researchers, working with U.S. collaborators, have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that appears to be responsible for hundreds of previously unexplained fever cases in China. The new pathogen, named Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), belongs to the genus Orthonairovirus in the Nairoviridae family. The findings were published in The New England Journal of Medicine on Sept. 2. The University of Minnesota’s Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy (CIDRAP) also reported on the discovery. ALTNV infection is associated with a flu-like illness marked by fever, fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, and abnormal laboratory results. The researchers also found evidence that co-infection with ALTNV and Dabie bandavirus (DBV) can lead to more serious illness. How Virus Was Found The discovery began with a medical mystery. In some parts of China, more than 30 percent of patients with symptoms resembling severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) test negative for DBV, the virus known to cause the disease. SFTS is a tick-borne illness that can cause high fever and dangerously low platelet counts. Its reported case-fatality rate is between 10 and 30 percent. The unexplained cases suggested that another pathogen might be circulating. Researchers collected samples from patients with fever and a history of tick exposure at sentinel hospitals in areas of China where tick-borne diseases are common. They used RNA sequencing and virus-isolation techniques to identify the pathogen. Genetic analysis placed ALTNV in the Orthonairovirus genus. Its amino acid sequence was less than 80.04 percent identical to those of other known species in the genus, supporting its classification as a distinct virus. The researchers tested 3,163 patients with fever and a history of tick exposure. Overall, 10.4 percent tested positive for ALTNV based on detection of viral RNA or antibodies. Among patients who had tested negative for DBV, 15.1 percent were positive for ALTNV. Patients infected only with ALTNV generally developed an influenza-like illness. Fatigue was reported in 84 percent of patients, gastrointestinal symptoms in 80 percent, low platelet counts in 38 percent, and elevated liver enzymes in 36 percent. All patients with ALTNV alone recovered without lasting complications. The picture was different among patients infected with both viruses. Of 38 patients with ALTNV and DBV coinfection, seven—18.4 percent—died. Coinfected patients also had higher rates of respiratory symptoms and impaired kidney function than patients infected with DBV alone. The Tick Behind the Virus The researchers also tested 47,428 ticks collected in 15 Chinese provinces. ALTNV RNA was detected in 1.29 percent of them, with the highest detection rate found in Haemaphysalis longicornis, commonly known as the Asian longhorned tick, at 1.75 percent. Laboratory experiments showed that H. longicornis can transmit ALTNV to mice. Infected mice developed tissue changes and produced antibodies against the virus. The findings provide evidence that ALTNV is a newly discovered emerging tick-borne virus associated with human illness. The researchers said the fact that ALTNV and DBV circulate in the same areas and share the same tick vector highlights the need for better testing to distinguish between the two infections. Chinese Military Scientists Included The study was led by seven researchers from Beijing's State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity, which is under the administration of Academy of Military Medical Sciences (AMMS). Two other authors are listed as directly affiliated with the AMMS, China's top-level military research institution. U.S. collaborators included Ellen Owen of the University of Washington and Jonathan E. Owen of Emory University. Potential Implications for US According to the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Asian longhorned tick has been found across much of the eastern United States, from New York south to Georgia and west to Missouri. The invasive species can heavily infest livestock and poses a potential threat to animal and human health by transmitting pathogens. However, the USDA currently has no evidence that ALTNV is circulating in U.S. tick populations or causing human infections in the United States

supplementary_news.content_title: New Tick-Borne Virus Discovered in China Traced to Hundreds of Fever Cases
supplementary_news.content: An Asian longhorned tick in July 2025. (Griffin Dill/University of Maine via AP) Chinese researchers, working with U.S. collaborators, have identified a previously unknown tick-borne virus that appears to be responsible for hundreds of previously unexplained fever cases in China. The new pathogen, named Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), belongs to the genus Orthonairovirus in the Nairoviridae family. The findings were published in The New England Journal of Medicine on Sept. 2. The University of Minnesota’s Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy (CIDRAP) also reported on the discovery. ALTNV infection is associated with a flu-like illness marked by fever, fatigue, gastrointestinal symptoms, and abnormal laboratory results. The researchers also found evidence that co-infection with ALTNV and Dabie bandavirus (DBV) can lead to more serious illness. How Virus Was Found The discovery began with a medical mystery. In some parts of China, more than 30 percent of patients with symptoms resembling severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) test negative for DBV, the virus known to cause the disease. SFTS is a tick-borne illness that can cause high fever and dangerously low platelet counts. Its reported case-fatality rate is between 10 and 30 percent. The unexplained cases suggested that another pathogen might be circulating. Researchers collected samples from patients with fever and a history of tick exposure at sentinel hospitals in areas of China where tick-borne diseases are common. They used RNA sequencing and virus-isolation techniques to identify the pathogen. Genetic analysis placed ALTNV in the Orthonairovirus genus. Its amino acid sequence was less than 80.04 percent identical to those of other known species in the genus, supporting its classification as a distinct virus. The researchers tested 3,163 patients with fever and a history of tick exposure. Overall, 10.4 percent tested positive for ALTNV based on detection of viral RNA or antibodies. Among patients who had tested negative for DBV, 15.1 percent were positive for ALTNV. Patients infected only with ALTNV generally developed an influenza-like illness. Fatigue was reported in 84 percent of patients, gastrointestinal symptoms in 80 percent, low platelet counts in 38 percent, and elevated liver enzymes in 36 percent. All patients with ALTNV alone recovered without lasting complications. The picture was different among patients infected with both viruses. Of 38 patients with ALTNV and DBV coinfection, seven—18.4 percent—died. Coinfected patients also had higher rates of respiratory symptoms and impaired kidney function than patients infected with DBV alone. The Tick Behind the Virus The researchers also tested 47,428 ticks collected in 15 Chinese provinces. ALTNV RNA was detected in 1.29 percent of them, with the highest detection rate found in Haemaphysalis longicornis, commonly known as the Asian longhorned tick, at 1.75 percent. Laboratory experiments showed that H. longicornis can transmit ALTNV to mice. Infected mice developed tissue changes and produced antibodies against the virus. The findings provide evidence that ALTNV is a newly discovered emerging tick-borne virus associated with human illness. The researchers said the fact that ALTNV and DBV circulate in the same areas and share the same tick vector highlights the need for better testing to distinguish between the two infections. Chinese Military Scientists Included The study was led by seven researchers from Beijing's State Key Laboratory of Pathogen and Biosecurity, which is under the administration of Academy of Military Medical Sciences (AMMS). Two other authors are listed as directly affiliated with the AMMS, China's top-level military research institution. U.S. collaborators included Ellen Owen of the University of Washington and Jonathan E. Owen of Emory University. Potential Implications for US According to the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), the Asian longhorned tick has been found across much of the eastern United States, from New York south to Georgia and west to Missouri. The invasive species can heavily infest livestock and poses a potential threat to animal and human health by transmitting pathogens. However, the USDA currently has no evidence that ALTNV is circulating in U.S. tick populations or causing human infections in the United States. Conversation 1 Comments Conversations are moderated.
